close_reason: Replaced 7 verbose 'iter().map(|id| Value::String((*id).to_owned())).collect()' sites with 'iter().copied().map(serde_json::Value::from).collect()'. Behaviourally equivalent (Value::from(&str) yields Value::String). 36/36 calendars-client tests pass. Commit 39eb335.
description:
Pattern appears verbatim in 5 places:
- calendar.rs:101-105
- event.rs:110-114
- event_notification.rs:95-99
- event_parse.rs:36-41
- participant_identity.rs:88-92
- principal_availability.rs:48-53

```
serde_json::Value::Array(
    d.into_iter()
        .map(|id| serde_json::Value::String(id.to_owned()))
        .collect(),
)
```

Where `d: Vec<&str>`, `id: &&str` (one extra ref because into_iter on Vec<&str> yields &str by value, not &&str — let me re-check). Actually `into_iter` on `Vec<&str>` yields `&str`, so `id: &str` and `id.to_owned()` is correct. Idiomatic alternative is more concise:

```
serde_json::Value::Array(d.into_iter().map(serde_json::Value::from).collect())
```

(`Value::from(&str)` exists and produces Value::String.) Or even shorter:

```
d.iter().copied().collect::<Vec<_>>().into() // serde_json::Value: From<Vec<&str>>
```

Minor — but 5 copies of the same boilerplate when one line would do. Section: idiomatic Rust / clippy-level.
title: into_iter().map(|id| Value::String(id.to_owned())).collect() — to_owned on &str is unnecessary
